Plaintiff firm M/s Ram Ratan Das Banarashi Lal filed the aforesaid suit on the allegations, inter alia, that on 5.1.1955 defendant No. 2 seized 12 items of goods from his godown at Kushtia Bazar as per detention memo Ext. 1 on suspicion; that at the time of the seizure as well as before the Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs sufficient proof as to their lawful possession by the plaintiff was placed but they totally ignored them; that out of the 12 items of goods seized 4 items namely 120 bags of bidi leaves, 9 bags of Dhup, 34. bags of catcchu and 958 bundles of coir strings were confiscated by order dated 3.9.1955 of the Collector of Central Excise and Land Customs, Chittagong Ext. 2(b); that the plaintiff purchased 120 bags of bidi leaves on 25.11.54 vide Ext. 21(1) from Nabi Hossain who auction purchased the same on 10.11.54 from Railway Lost Property office Santahar; that the plaintiff purchased 5 bags of Dhup from M/s SN Gupta & Co. on 23.2.57 vide Ext. 19. 11 bags of Dhup from M/s. TP Khetwat on 10.12.57 vide Ext. 19(a), 6 bags of Dhup from BB Shaha & Brothers on 10.8.59 BS-26.11.52 vide Ext 31 and 3 bags in police auction Kushtia on 24.10.54 Ext. 34 & 34(a) and after gradual sales there remained 9 bags which were seized: that the plaintiff purchased 15 bags of catechu on 12.5.54 Ext. 19(b), 25 bags of catecheu on 11.7.54 Ext. 19(c), 8 bags catechu on 19.7.54 Ext. 19(g), 44 bags of catechu on. 7.11.54 Ext. 19(e), 11 bags of catechu on 11.11.54 Ext. 19(d), and 24 bags of catechu on 18.11.54 Ext. 19(f) from their commission agent Jain company who purchased the same from various importers such as Dada Limited & others and out of the same 24 bags were damaged due to sinking of boat, 69 bags sold and remaining 34 bags were seized; that the plaintiff purchased 55 bundles of coir strings each from Biswanath Singh on 17.5.54 Ext. 21, Tarapada Saha on 17.5.54 Ext. 21(a), Banat All on 18.5.54 Ext. 21(b), Bishnu Ghosh on 18.5.54 Ext. 21(c) and 50 bundles each from Aditya Kumar on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(d). Fanindra Nath Roy on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(c) Atair Ram on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(f) and Harendra Nath Saha on 20.5.54 Ext. 21(g), 450 bundles from Maliram Agarwalla on 1.7.54 Ext. 25 and 475 bundles from Nabi Hossain on 25.11.54 Ext. 21(h); that the aforesaid 8 persons imported 420 bundles without import permit in contravention of import restriction and got the same released on payment of penalty, etc. as per order dated' 10.3.54 Ext. 4(a), that Maliram Agarwalla imported 450 bundles without import permit in contravention of import restriction and got the, same released on payment of penalty, etc. as per order dated 26.10.53 Ext. 24; that Nabi Hossain auction purchased 475 bundles from Railway Lost Property office, Santahar on 5.11.54, 8.11.54 and 10.11.54 Ext. 25(a) to 25(c); that the aforesaid persons brought the said goods through Railway; that out of 1345 bundles 387 bundles were sold and remaining 958 bundles were seized; that the said goods purchased by the plaintiff were either duty paid or duty free and plaintiff's possession was neither illegal nor unauthorized as the same were imported either under valid licence from whom plaintiff purchased the same or plaintiff purchased the same from auction purchasers; that plaintiff's possession of the said goods did not come within the mischief of section 167(81) of the Sea Customs Act 1878 read with section 3(3) of the Import Export (Control) Act 1950; that plaintiff filed an appeal before the Central Board of Revenue against Collector's order of confiscation of the said goods and the said appeal was wrongly rejected on 25.6.56 Ext. 2 and thereafter plaintiff filed a revision before the central government and by order dated 11.10.56 said revision was also rejected vide Ext. 2(a). 

 11. Under order dated 3.9.55 Collector of Customs confiscated the suit goods under section 167 (81) of the Sea Customs Act, 1878 read with section 9 of the Land Customs Act, 1924 and under section 3(3) of the Import and Export (Control) Act. 1950. Plaintiff preferred an appeal to the Central Board of Revenue against the said order of the Collector and by order dated 25.6.56 the said appeal was rejected. Plaintiff then filed a Revisional application before the Central Government and by order dated 11.10.56 the said revisional application was also rejected. Section 9 of the Land Customs Act, 1924 provides that the provisions of Sea Customs Act, 1878 for the purpose of levy of duties of Land Customs and trial of offences shall apply. Section 188 of the Sea Customs Act provides that "Every order passed in appeal under this Act shall subject to the power of revision conferred by section 191 be final". We are to see whether in the above facts and circumstances and position of law plaintiff-respondent's suit was maintainable or not or the court below had any jurisdiction to entertain and decide the same.
